questions.question: What is the density of $X\sim\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda)$?
What condition is required for the exponential rate $\lambda$?
What does the exponential distribution model?
options: The number of events in a fixed window of time
The number of trials needed for a first success
Waiting time to the next event, constant rate

questions.question: What is $E[X]$ for $X\sim\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda)$?
What is $\operatorname{Var}(X)$ for $X\sim\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda)$?
Which situation may be modeled exponentially?
options: Time to the next call at a constant rate.
The number of calls in an hour at a constant rate.
Number of tosses until the first heads.
Time to failure of a part that wears out with age.

questions.question: If $X\sim\operatorname{Exp}(2)$, what is $E[X]$?
If $X\sim\operatorname{Exp}(2)$, what is $\operatorname{Var}(X)$?
Which value is outside the support of an exponential random variable?
In a Poisson process, what distribution do interarrival times have?
How is the exponential distribution connected to memorylessness?
options: One of many continuous distributions with the memoryless property.
The continuous distribution with the memoryless property.
The discrete distribution with the memoryless property.
A distribution that is memoryless only when $\lambda=1$.

questions.question: Why does a higher exponential rate imply shorter typical waiting time?
What is the relationship between exponential waiting time and a constant hazard assumption?
options: A constant hazard gives a waiting time uniform on an interval
A constant hazard means failures become likelier with age
A constant hazard can lead to exponential time until failure
A constant hazard gives a Poisson-distributed time until failure

questions.question: If $X\sim\operatorname{Exp}(5)$, what is the density at $x=0$?
At rate $\lambda=4$, what is the standard deviation of an exponential waiting time?
Which model is appropriate for time until radioactive decay under a constant rate?
Why is the exponential distribution continuous rather than discrete?
options: It models waiting time over a continuum.
It counts arrivals in a fixed time interval.
Its rate $\lambda$ may take any positive real value.
Its density is continuous at every point $x$.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes Poisson arrival counts from exponential waiting times?
options: Exponential counts arrivals; Poisson models interarrival time.
Both count arrivals; the exponential does so in continuous time.
Poisson counts arrivals; exponential models interarrival time.
Poisson counts arrivals; exponential models the $n$th arrival time.

questions.question: An exponential waiting-time distribution is proposed with rate parameter $\lambda=-1$. Why is this parameter value invalid?
options: The exponential rate must be positive
The rate must lie between $0$ and $1$
Only the variance $1/\lambda^2$ needs to be positive
Negative $\lambda$ only flips the support to $x<0$

questions.question: If two exponential models have rates $1$ and $3$, which has the shorter mean waiting time?
